pge.fixed: Base Services Charge, billed by the day: 79.343¢ a day for most homes (about $24 a month), 39.688¢ for income tier 2, 19.713¢ for income tier 1.

plans.name: E-1, Residential Services (tiered)
plans.about: The price steps up once a home passes its baseline allowance for the season and climate zone.
plans.basis: Total bundled rates, effective 1 June 2026, Advice 7921-E, Decision D.26-04-036.

plans.name: E-TOU-C, time of use, peak 4–9 p.m. every day
plans.about: The price depends on the hour and the season. Usage inside the baseline allowance gets a credit of 8.140¢/kWh.
plans.basis: Total bundled rates, effective 1 June 2026, Advice 7921-E, Decision D.26-04-036.

pge.note: The filed schedules also list a California Climate Credit of $36.18 per household, which the current sheets place in the August and September bill cycles.

changes.what: PG&E’s 2027 general rate case (A.25-05-009) asks for $16.637 billion of revenue in 2027, an increase of $1.237 billion or 8%, and 6.1% more in each of 2028 to 2030. The CPUC’s fact sheet puts a typical combined gas and electric residential bill up 3.6% in 2027 against 2025.

sce.fixed: Base Services Charge, billed by the day: about $24.15 a month for most homes, $12 for FERA and $6 for CARE customers, according to SCE.
sce.note: SCE’s plan prices change often and its tariff book is the place to read them; we show only what we could re-check. SCE states an average residential rate of 34.5¢ per kWh from 1 October 2026, or 33.3¢ counting the Climate Credit.

changes.what: SCE’s average residential rate moved from 34.4¢ to 34.5¢ per kWh. SCE describes it as the net result of Woolsey Fire revenue increases, offset by decreases elsewhere.

The CPUC decided SCE’s 2025 general rate case (A.23-05-010): a 2025 base revenue requirement of $9.664 billion, up 12.61%. At 500 kWh a month, the non-CARE bill rises $15.52 (9.1%) and the CARE bill $9.79 (9.1%).

plans.name: Schedule RS, Residential Service (North Carolina)
plans.about: One price per kWh before riders. Riders are added on top, which is why the all-in average above is higher.
plans.basis: Leaf No. 11, effective 1 January 2026, NCUC Docket E-7, Subs 1276 and 1325.

duke-energy-carolinas.note: South Carolina homes are billed under a separate South Carolina schedule, not shown here.

changes.when: Settlement reported July 2026, not approved when last checked
changes.what: A settlement in Duke Energy Carolinas’ North Carolina rate case would raise residential rates 5.9% in 2027 and 3.6% in 2028, with a return on equity of 9.8% against the 10.95% requested. It needs Utilities Commission approval, and not every party signed.
